title: Pipe-flow bench data recalibrates the dose model: aim for a ~13 mm throat
tldr: Your 7 current-part curves on steady pipe flow fit chlorine flow ∝ suction^0.73 to within 5%. With that law the current part is already fairly consistent on piped flow (1.3–1.5× from 6 to 38 L/min); its real problem is handpump overflow. The flattest possible fixed shape spans 6–100 L/min at about 1.6×, with a throat of about 13 mm, so round 1 was redirected from 14–18 mm to 12.5–16 mm.
body: p

How the fit works: the 3-D CFD of the current part gives its port suction at every flow. If chlorine flow goes as suction^n, the dose goes as suction^n ÷ flow. Each device gets its own scale (needle setting), and one n is fitted to all seven curves.
list
Best n = 0.73 (range 0.69–0.77), rms error 5%.
n = 1 (fully viscous needle valve, my earlier assumption): 29% error. n = 0.5 (orifice): 25%.
The model reproduces the measured shape: dose high at 6 L/min (×1.32 vs measured 1.24–1.40), lowest near 15, rising to ×1.23 at 38 (measured 1.16–1.47).
p
What changes:
list
Corrected: the current part's piped spread is 1.3× over 6–38 L/min (1.96× extrapolated to 100), not the 5.8× I posted earlier under n = 1.
Ranking flips: V1 1.83×, V2 2.43×, V3 3.12× over 6–100 L/min. Large throats are now the worst, because the water column below the port over-feeds at low flow.

Best possible fixed Venturi (suction = column + k·Q²): about 1.6× over 6–100 L/min when column ÷ k ≈ 180. In the 1" V-layout that means a throat of about 13–13.5 mm. A 13 mm throat should overflow the handpump only above about 25 L/min (between V12 at 22.9 and V1 above 30).
p

Round 1 redirected without stopping anything: the 17 and 18 mm shapes were dropped, and 12.5, 13 and 13.5 mm throats (each with 26, 23 and 20 mm outlets) were added on the 4 spare cores. Next round will vary the port position, which sets the column, around the column ÷ k ≈ 180 target.

title: Round 1 shape screen running; current part added for comparison
tldr: [Superseded in part by the 16:30 bench-data update: the piped-flow numbers here assumed chlorine flow ∝ suction; the measured law is suction^0.73.] 15 new bore shapes are being simulated at 7 flows from 6 to 120 L/min (105 cases). The first cases are finishing cleanly; the full ranking is due about 10 pm tonight. The existing part is now shown next to every new design on this site.
body: p

Round 1 varies two things: throat diameter (14, 15, 16, 17, 18 mm) and outlet diameter (26 mm as V1–V3, or a short contraction to 23 or 20 mm). Everything else is held at the V1 layout: 1" inlet, 20° inlet cone, 14 mm long throat, port 7 mm down the throat, 4° diffuser, 125 mm body.
p

Why the outlet contraction: at 6 L/min almost all the port suction comes from the water column below the port. That column only exists if the outlet runs full. In a 26 mm outlet at 6 L/min the water moves down about as fast as an air bubble rises, so air can creep in. A 20–23 mm outlet keeps it full, and it also trims suction at high flow, which flattens the dose.
list
Pipeline check: the 2-D setup re-ran V1 at 30 L/min and matched the earlier result to every digit (level 1.833 cm, port −5.116 kPa).
Independent agent audit: all 15 shapes match the intended geometry to 0.005 mm; all meshes pass checkMesh (non-orthogonality 20°, 51–54k cells); wall cells stay fine enough (y+ ≈ 1) up to 120 L/min.
Speed: about 46 min per case with 12 running at once; done about 10 pm.
p

Current part, for reference (3-D, its own 3/4" E-Sig + elbow train): it overflows the Afridev at about 18.5 L/min, and on piped flow its dose varies 3.4× over 6–60 L/min (about 5.8× extrapolated to 100). Every new candidate is measured against it and against V1.

title: New goal: steady piped dosing from 6 to 100+ L/min, bore shape only
tldr: [Superseded in part by the 16:30 bench-data update: the piped-flow numbers here assumed chlorine flow ∝ suction; the measured law is suction^0.73.] The redesign now targets consistent dosing on piped flow from 6 to over 100 L/min, a working dose at 6 L/min, and no handpump overflow, changing only the Venturi bore. Of the existing designs V2 (16 mm) is the most even; the best throat looks like 16.5–17 mm.
body: p

Dose consistency on piped flow depends on how port suction grows with flow. Suction has two parts: the water column below the port (about 1 kPa, independent of flow) and a throat term that grows with flow². The needle valve passes bleach at about 1 mL/min, a viscous flow, so chlorine flow is proportional to suction and dose is proportional to suction ÷ flow.
list
Small throats (V1, 14 mm): the flow² term dominates early, so they overdose at high flow (dose spread 3.3× over 6–100 L/min).
Large throats (V3, 18 mm): the column dominates, so they underdose at low flow (2.5×).
Best balance for 6–100 L/min: column ≈ 600 × throat coefficient, about a 16.5–17 mm throat, spread about 2.2×. That fits the 0.3–0.8 mg/L band at one needle setting (2.67×).
p
Excluded on the user's call: any added part (flap, valve, vent, riser). The vent two-phase run was stopped at 0.33 s.

title: Narrow throats V10–V12 complete: they overflow inside the handpump range
tldr: Five designs at nine flows (6–30 L/min) in 3-D, all converged. Narrower throats give more suction but back the water up: V10 overflows at 14.8 L/min, V11t at 20.5, V12 at 22.9. No fixed throat keeps the Venturi full and below overflow from 10 to 20 L/min on the handpump.
body: p

The handpump window is set by two levels in the pump head: above the inlet bore top (+2.2 cm) the Venturi stays full; above +5.8 cm the Afridev overflows. Level rises with flow², so any fixed shape stays in that window over a flow ratio of only about 1.08×. Shape moves the window; it can't widen it.
p
V1 already doses within the acceptable 0.1–1.5 mg/L on the bench from 7 to 26 L/min, so the new design must not raise the level much above V1's.

title: Two-phase handpump simulation: why dosing drops at low pump rates
tldr: V1 at 80 clicks/min (13.2 L/min): the pump head drains, and once the level falls below the top of the inlet bore, air runs along the bore into the Venturi. Suction is lost for part of every stroke and the dose falls to about half.
body: list
Suction weakens at 2.72 s; the port goes dry at 2.73 s; the outlet stops running full at 2.76 s.
After air reaches the Venturi the solver's time step falls ~10× (bubbly flow).
This explains the bench result: 0.31 mg/L at 6.9 L/min vs 1.32 at 19.5 L/min.
